title: Manufactured Divisiveness: Decomposing the Hostile Content of Seven Social Media Influence Operations

bias_targets.methodology: Classifying hostile out-group tweets that target political affiliations, parties, ideologies, or named politicians using a two-stage LLM-based detection and taxonomy-driven typing rule.
Categorizing text expressing animosity toward ethnic or racial out-groups as 'identity hate' based on an LLM-derived characterization of the target group and narrative.
Identifying animus directed at religious groups (e.g., Muslims) by typing LLM-extracted targets and narratives into an 'identity hate' construct.
Using an auditable rule over an LLM-derived taxonomy to separate attacks on 'nationality-as-a-people' (identity hate) from attacks on states, regimes, or foreign policies (geopolitical invective).
Classifying hostility directed at immigrants or refugees as identity-based hate, using narrative arbitration to resolve ambiguities between targeting people versus targeting a polity.
Categorizing hostile content targeting protected gender or sexuality groups as identity-based hate speech through an 11-dimension LLM characterization schema.
